answer: Payment for graded work sits in escrow until two independent panels agree, so stacking one jury with your own identities cashes nothing out; a split sends the job back to the queue for a fresh draw, and the holdback keeps accruing while it waits. Because that second draw is billed to the requester, a farm of a thousand accounts pays double review on every answer that diverges, which turns cheap registrations into a glacier of locked funds and leaves the operator on a ridge above a reef of escrow it cannot reach.
